sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].

The path was cyclical rather than steady: a 20.4% jump in FY2018 to $54.7 billion [F3][D92], a 22.4% collapse in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], then a 12.8% rise in FY2023 to $67.1 billion [F8][D357].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
FY2023's gain was primarily favorable price realization and higher sales volume, with dealer inventory up about $2.1 billion during the year [P32].
North America supplied the latest year's growth, contributing 3.4pp of the 4.3% increase on a 54.2% revenue share [D515][D463][D513].
North America sales rose 6% on higher sales volume, mainly higher sales of equipment to end users, partly offset by unfavorable price realization [P12].
Power & Energy carried the segment story, contributing 5.2pp on 11.6% growth, while Construction Industries subtracted 0.6pp [D759][D758][D766].
Construction Industries' $395 million decline was primarily unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume of $568 million [P8].
Operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 9.1%, and operating income fell 14.7% against revenue growth of 4.3% [D489][D481][D464][D463].
The FY2025 operating margin of 16.5% sat 2.2pp above the 14.3% window median but 3.7pp below the FY2024 high of 20.2% [F30][D1123][F29][D476].
Cost of revenue took 4.2pp off the margin, while R&D added 0.1pp and SG&A was flat [D490][D491][D492].

The operating profit decline was primarily unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin, a gap the pack puts at 3.4pp [F50][F30][D1168].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025, above the 1.16x window median, and free cash flow of $8.9 billion was 1.00x [F80][F40][D450][D1158][F100][D451].
Free cash flow margin of 13.2% was above the 11.9% window median but below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D447][D1129][D1128].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F90][D470][D446][D452].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion primarily on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Net debt stood at $26.2 billion in FY2025, with net cash of -38.8% of revenue, cash of $10.0 billion and a 1.44x current ratio [D456][D457][F140][F180].
That net-cash ratio ranked at the 67th percentile of three industrials peers against a -59.4% median [D1169][D1170].
The pack's total debt omits long-term debt due within one year, which the filer reports at $7.1 billion in FY2025, so the net debt figure understates borrowings [R7][X180][D455].
Buybacks of $5.2 billion plus dividends of $2.7 billion equaled 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D459][D483].
Long-term debt due within one year is in no line of the pack across FY2016-FY2025, running $5.3 billion to $9.1 billion a year and $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7][X180].
Every net-debt and total-debt figure here is therefore a partial measure, and the leverage picture is worse than the table shows [R7][D456].
Net debt rose for a second year in FY2025, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 to $24.9 billion in FY2024 and $26.2 billion in FY2025 [R1][D350][D403][D456].
Debt-funded capital return while operating profit falls is the pattern to watch, though the omitted current maturities make the level uncertain [R1][D464].
Net income for FY2021-FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, differing by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to margins and cash conversion, but the 10-K figure should be used where precision matters [R3][X20].
Whether the FY2026 10-K shows operating margin recovering above the 14.3% window median or falling further from the 16.5% FY2025 level [D1123][F30].
Whether capex stays above the 1.25x D&A ratio of FY2025 or falls back toward the 0.92x of FY2024 [D452][D399].
Whether net debt, on the pack's basis, moves back below the $24.9 billion FY2024 level or extends past $26.2 billion [D403][D456].
